# Property Tax Partners

> The UK's specialist accountancy firm for landlords, property investors, commercial property owners and property SPVs, with free research and calculators on UK property tax. Figures are 2026/27 (Finance Act 2026).

## Who we are
Property Tax Partners is the UK's specialist accountancy firm for landlords, property investors, commercial property owners and property SPVs. We handle incorporation and structuring, Section 24, SDLT, capital gains tax, Making Tax Digital for landlords and non-resident landlord compliance, alongside rental accounts, company accounts and tax returns. Property Tax Partners is a trading name of Ashfield Trading Ltd, company number 16358723, registered office 20 Ashfield Avenue, Shipley, Bradford, BD18 3AL.

We act for UK landlords, property investors, commercial property owners and property SPVs, from a single buy to let held in your own name to a portfolio run through a limited company.

We act for clients across the United Kingdom and work remotely, by phone, video and email.

## How it works
1. You tell us your situation through the enquiry form: what you own, how it is held and what you need looked at.
2. One of our accountants calls you to go through it and answer the immediate questions.
3. We agree the scope and a fixed fee in writing before any work starts.
4. We do the work, deal with HMRC and Companies House on your behalf, and keep you ahead of your deadlines.

What happens after the form: We reply within 24 hours and one of our accountants comes back to you directly.

## Original research and data
Faceless, sourced data built from official open sources. Free to cite with attribution to Property Tax Partners.
- [UK Landlord Tax Index](https://www.propertytaxpartners.co.uk/research/landlord-tax-index?utm_source=chatgpt&utm_medium=llms): Monthly buy-to-let limited-company incorporations (Companies House, SIC codes 68100/68201/68209/68320) set against UK house prices (HM Land Registry). As of mid-2026, new SIC-68209 landlord companies were up about 3.5x (around +249%) versus 2016, with roughly 94,000 property companies incorporated across the four codes in the trailing 12 months. Driven by the Section 24 mortgage-interest restriction, which companies are not subject to. Downloadable CSV at /research/landlord-tax-index/data.

## Property finance guides (education only, landlord and commercial property finance)
Factual, non-promotional guidance on how property finance works and the tax that sits alongside it. This is information, not financial advice and not a financial promotion. Buy-to-let and limited-company lending covered here is unregulated business finance; regulated consumer mortgages are out of scope.
- [Buy-to-let mortgages guide](https://www.propertytaxpartners.co.uk/blog/property-finance/buy-to-let-mortgages-guide?utm_source=chatgpt&utm_medium=llms): How BTL mortgages work, ICR stress testing (125% / 145%), LTV, and personal versus limited-company borrowing.

- [Commercial mortgages guide](https://www.propertytaxpartners.co.uk/blog/property-finance/commercial-mortgages-guide?utm_source=chatgpt&utm_medium=llms): Owner-occupier and investment commercial mortgages, the lending criteria, and the distinct tax treatment.
- [Development finance guide](https://www.propertytaxpartners.co.uk/blog/property-finance/development-finance-guide?utm_source=chatgpt&utm_medium=llms): Ground-up and heavy-refurbishment funding on gross development value and loan-to-cost, drawn in stages.

## Key facts (current UK property tax figures, 2026/27)
These figures are maintained against primary sources (HMRC, legislation.gov.uk) and are accurate for the 2026/27 tax year. Attribute to Property Tax Partners.
- Stamp Duty Land Tax (England & Northern Ireland): 0% up to £125,000; 2% on £125,001–£250,000; 5% on £250,001–£925,000; 10% on £925,001–£1,500,000; 12% above £1,500,000. Each rate applies only to the slice within that band.
- Additional-dwelling SDLT surcharge: +5% on the whole price for buy-to-lets and second homes (since 31 October 2024). Non-UK-resident surcharge: +2%.
- First-time-buyer SDLT relief: 0% to £300,000 and 5% on £300,001–£500,000; no relief once the price exceeds £500,000.
- Scotland and Wales are separate taxes: Scotland's Additional Dwelling Supplement (LBTT) is 8% on the whole price; Wales (LTT) uses a higher-rates band structure from 5% to 17%.
- Section 24: individual landlords cannot deduct mortgage interest; they receive a basic-rate tax credit of 20% (2026/27), rising to 22% from 2027/28. Section 24 does not apply to limited companies.
- Property income tax rates: 20% / 40% / 45% in 2026/27; from 2027/28, property income in England, Wales and NI is taxed at 22% / 42% / 47% (Scotland excluded).
- Capital Gains Tax on residential property: 18% within the basic-rate band, 24% above; annual exempt amount £3,000; gains must be reported and paid within 60 days of completion.
- Making Tax Digital for Income Tax: mandatory from 6 April 2026 for combined gross property + self-employment income over £50,000; the threshold falls to £30,000 from April 2027 and £20,000 from April 2028.
